items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Albert Snyder said he'd go with me.

ctx.x: NO, I had an alto by now. I had gotten an alto and it was a York alto, another York alto.

Because I had to return this fellow's C melody. So I made it up -- of course, a lot of the older boys, Albert Snyder who was older than me, they used to do it for a lark, just get on a train, hobo to Chicago, hang around there for a few days and come back. So I got contact with him because I had never done it before. So he said, 'well, I'll go with you,' Albert Snyder said he'd go with me. So we had it all set up so that we would let Bill take the horn on the train and we'd both catch that same train that night…

Well, that day -- I used to divide my time with my grandmother who lived on the east side and my mother who lived on the west side. So this day I told my grandmother that I would stay with my mother that night and I got up and put on my suit, which was a common thing, put my overalls over my suit, and I went onto the west side. And after supper I told my mother I was going over to stay with my grandmother.
